findings.problem: TODO comment declares intent to use Rayon and SmallVec because 'it will be faster' — a textbook cargo-cult decision for a fixed `[u8; 4]` input. Rayon parallelism on 4 elements is orders of magnitude slower due to thread-dispatch overhead. SmallVec is unnecessary without a measured small-size distribution showing heap avoidance is needed.
findings.failure_mode: Adding Rayon will introduce massive overhead for a 4-element input, making the function measurably slower. Adding SmallVec adds compile-time and runtime complexity with no measured benefit on this workload size.
findings.fix: Remove the TODO. For 4 fixed elements, keep the current sequential iterator approach or replace Vec with [Option<&'static str>; 4] or SmallVec<[&'static str; 4]> only if a benchmark proves heap allocation is a measured bottleneck.

findings.problem: Returns Vec for a known-bounded capacity of 4 elements with no try_reserve or allocation-failure handling. Allocation failure on this path is part of the contract and must be handled explicitly per Holzman allocation rules.
findings.failure_mode: On memory pressure, the allocation can OOM the process instead of returning a typed AllocationError, violating the no-panic contract.
findings.fix: Replace Vec with SmallVec<[&'static str; 4]> to eliminate heap allocation entirely, or if Vec is retained, return Result<SmallVec<[&'static str; 4]>, AllocationError> with try_reserve and checked arithmetic.

findings.problem: Returns heap-allocated Vec for a deterministic pure computation on 4 known elements. The pure core should avoid intermediate heap allocations when a stack/borrowed output is feasible.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap traffic degrades cache locality and introduces allocation overhead on every call, which is measurable in tight loops.
findings.fix: Return SmallVec<[&'static str; 4]> or use an output-buffer pattern (&mut [Option<&'static str>; 4]) to eliminate heap allocation. Benchmark to confirm.

findings.problem: The TODO makes a performance claim ('it will be faster') without any benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence. Holzman Rust requires measured evidence before using Rayon, SmallVec, or similar optimizations.
findings.failure_mode: Optimization decisions based on intuition rather than evidence lead to regressions. The folklore belief that Rayon is always faster is known to be false for tiny fixed-size inputs.
findings.fix: Add a microbenchmark (criterion or similar) comparing the current sequential approach against any proposed Rayon/SmallVec variant before making changes. Require the benchmark to show a measured improvement before merging.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated performance claim about Rayon/SmallVec
no profiler data for allocation patterns on classify_four
no allocation audit showing Vec vs SmallVec/stack trade-off for 4-element inputs
no second-ring evidence (Miri/Kani) to verify the pure computation has no UB
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The code itself has no unsafe/unwrap/expect/panic, but the TODO comment signals an imminent cargo-cult change that would introduce a performance regression. The Vec return for fixed 4-element input is a minor allocation inefficiency. Without benchmarks, the exact performance impact of any future change is unquantified.
